messages.author: 272fb71d6c54a687
messages.subject: Can MSStats do protein inference ?
parts:
Hi,

I'm interesting in analyzing DIA data exported from Skyline with MSStats. The library was created from search result using both SwissProt and TrEMBL database. This is necessary because SwissProt data for Rat is still quite incomplete. The problem with this is it included many similar protein sequence and therefore non-unique peptides. These non-unique peptides are important and cannot be simply excluded. If these peptides are added to one protein (? first matched protein entry), they may be incorrectly associated with proteins (compared with using razor peptide approach). So it would be great if I can associate these peptides with every matched proteins in Skyline and group proteins later in MSStats.

Thank you,
Kavee

messages.author: 2889aa2e61425c8e
messages.subject: Re: Can MSStats do protein inference ?
parts:
Dear Kavee,

MSstats does not implement peptide weighting for protein-level conclusions. You can trick MSstats into doing this by duplicating the peptides, altering their names, and mapping each of the altered names to a different protein. This way MSstats will think that these are uniquely mapped peptides. This is not great, of course, but something you can do in a short term.

HTH
Olga

Dear Olga,

Thank you for your response. I've just realized that UniProt also provides reference proteome which combined SwissProt and TrEMBL in non-redundant way (single protein sequence per gene). I believe using this would solve my problem.

Best,
